articles.title: Missouri's Eli Drinkwitz tried to embarrass Kansas with late score, bemoans Jayhawks making rivalry about Civil War
articles.summary: Drinkwitz doesn't see the point of the historic series continuing if Kansas, in his eyes, keeps turning it deeper than it needs to be on the gridiron.
articles.body:
Eli Drinkwitz doesn't usually mince words. While mostly affable, the Missouri head coach doesn't always subscribe to tact. He's not to afraid to say how he feels.

He certainly didn't pull any punches after his No. 23 Tigers squad humbled Kansas on the road Friday night in the latest iteration of the schools' "Border Showdown." Missouri (2-0) handed the Jayhawks (1-1) a 38-21 defeat that could have looked even more lopsided had a head-turning shot to the end zone not fallen incomplete in the game's waning moments at David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium in Lawrence.

That potential death knell resulted from Drinkwitz's frustration toward Kansas and the way the Jayhawks brazenly approached the programs' longstanding yet complicated rivalry in the lead-up to the matchup .

Kansas leaned into the Civil War history between the two states, posting a pregame hype video framed as "heroes vs. villains" with the social media caption, "It is that deep." Drinkwitz wasn't amused and fundamentally disagreed.

"I get there's a past to it, but why are we stirring that bull crap up? It's 9/11," Drinkwitz said postgame on Friday, the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 attacks.

"This country needs unity now more than ever. And I was embarrassed for 'em, to be honest."

Drinkwitz added, in reference to Missouri's pass that could have ran up the score with less than 30 seconds left: "And that's why I tried to embarrass them at the end."

Now in his seventh season at the helm of the Tigers, Drinkwitz expressed disappointment in "the turn" the fabled series between the neighboring programs took.

"I thought that was uncalled for," he said. "And this is about two teams playing football, and especially on 9/11 when we need more unity now than ever before — to be putting some stuff on your screen, celebrating ... I mean, everybody's got complicated pasts. "To make that an icon was bizarre to me. So I'm just glad that this whole right-versus-wrong bull crap that was started just got settled on a football field because it's a football game. It's a football game. It's an American football game that people love to come watch and cheer for their teams. "It's not any deeper than that."

"I thought that was uncalled for," he said. "And this is about two teams playing football, and especially on 9/11 when we need more unity now than ever before — to be putting some stuff on your screen, celebrating ... I mean, everybody's got complicated pasts.

"To make that an icon was bizarre to me. So I'm just glad that this whole right-versus-wrong bull crap that was started just got settled on a football field because it's a football game. It's a football game. It's an American football game that people love to come watch and cheer for their teams.

Kansas' aforementioned video, which was narrated by Jayhawks alum and former NFL defensive lineman Gilbert Brown , describes the "Border Showdown" like this:

"It's fueled by hatred passed down through generations," Brown said of the rivalry. "Our roots reach back to the Civil War when blood was spilled over what you believed in and which side you stood on. There are heroes and villains. Only allegiance decides their legacy. There's right and wrong. There's Kansas and Missouri."

Only the 1918 Spanish flu pandemic got in the way of Kansas and Missouri facing off on the gridiron between 1891 to 2011. For more than a century, their head-to-head was a staple in the college football landscape. But in 2012, Missouri left the Big 12 for the SEC, and the rivalry went dormant. Its 14-year hiatus ended last season, with the Tigers outlasting the Jayhawks in Columbia, Missouri .

Missouri leads the all-time series 59-54-9, according to Winsipedia , although the all-time record is a debate subject as well .

As Drinkwitz briefly conceded, "there's a past to" the series. The teams' nicknames come from the Civil War era. And the regional dispute can be traced back to the Kansas-Nebraska Act of 1854, which allowed the two then-territories to vote on their status as free or slave states when they joined the Union. Conflict ensued on the border of Kansas and Missouri — a slave state at the time — as pro-slavery and anti-slavery forces clashed.

That period of violent guerrilla warfare is known as "Bleeding Kansas." It served as a precursor to the Civil War.

"I don't really care if it continues or not," Drinkwitz said, when asked about the football rivalry, which isn't scheduled to pick back up again until 2031.

"I mean, if they're going to be weird about it, then what's the point?" he said. "If they want to have a football game and play a football game and have a great rivalry on the border, then awesome, let's do it. But if we want to make it deeper than that, man, we left Kansas bleeding again, so call it good."

Missouri broke open Friday's game in the second half, converting a pair of Robert Woodyard Jr. takeaways into touchdowns.

The game was the series' first in Kansas since 2005. It nearly ended with one more Tigers touchdown.

"I mean, I didn't want to score too bad, or I'd have called timeouts and tried," Drinkwitz said postgame after being asked how badly he wanted to score late.

"But I just wanted to — I mean, we didn't think we were going to throw that in the end zone, but I just wanted to let them know, like, 'Dude, what are y'all doing?' This is a football game. It shouldn't be bigger than that."

articles.title: Danny Jordaan reelected head of South African soccer association while facing fraud charges
articles.summary: The head organizer of the 2010 World Cup was reelected president of South Africa's soccer federation on Saturday despite facing criminal charges over alleged...
articles.body:
CAPE TOWN, South Africa (AP) — The head organizer of the 2010 World Cup was reelected president of South Africa's soccer federation on Saturday despite facing criminal charges over alleged fraud while in office.

Danny Jordaan, 75, beat challenger Sandile Zungu, a South African businessman and soccer club owner, by 157 votes to 82, according to an announcement by the South African Football Association. Jordaan has been head of SAFA since 2013 and will serve a fourth term.

Jordaan was a pivotal figure in bringing the World Cup to Africa for the first time in 2010 and his work was praised in helping make the tournament a success.

But he has been followed by controversy since then.

He came under scrutiny in 2015 over if he had knowledge of an alleged $10 million bribe made by South Africa to a FIFA official to help win the 2010 hosting rights. The allegation against unidentified South African bid officials was contained in an indictment by the U.S. Department of Justice. South Africa denied the allegation.

Jordaan was accused in 2017 of rape by South African singer and political activist Jennifer Ferguson, who said the rape happened more than two decades earlier. Jordaan denied that allegation, and charges against him were dropped because of a lack of evidence.

Jordaan was arrested in 2024 and charged with fraud and theft for the alleged misuse of around $70,000 while SAFA president. He was accused alongside several others, including a former acting CEO of SAFA and the chief financial officer of SAFA.

The charges accuse Jordaan of using SAFA money to hire personal security and a PR company to enhance his public image in the wake of the Ferguson rape allegations.

The fraud case has been bogged down by delays and is yet to go to trial. Jordaan and his co-accused denied wrongdoing.

The buildup to Saturday's SAFA election was also troubled, with the national association saying some voting officials had received death threats and others had been harassed and intimidated. SAFA said it would notify the police but didn't say who was behind the threats.

Three of the four teams that reached the third round of the Bundesliga with a 100% record were in action on Saturday morning (12).

And two of them picked up another win, remaining tied at the top of the table.

Borussia Dortmund beat newly promoted Paderborn, while Freiburg thrashed Borussia Mönchengladbach .

The exception was Augsburg , who started the day in first place but conceded a late equalizer against Bayer Leverkusen .

Elversberg could also end the round with nine points from three matches, as they face Bayern Munich this Sunday (13).

See below for details of this Saturday morning's Bundesliga matches:

It was not Guirassy's day to be the goalscorer.

Dortmund's No. 9 had two goals ruled out for offside in the first half. In the second half, he was denied by the opposing goalkeeper.

But it was his assist that set up Fábio Silva to open the scoring.

Felix Nmecha sealed the win with two goals late on.

Six wins in six matches played. That is how Freiburg's season has started.

In addition to their three Bundesliga matches, the run includes one German Cup game and two Conference League matches.

Gladbach, on the other hand, are still without a point in the league.

The scoreline suggests a comfortable win, but goalkeeper Noah Atubolu played a very important role.

He saved a penalty taken by Mainz when the score was still 1-0 and extended an impressive record.

This was the SIXTH consecutive penalty saved by Atubolu, who was signed by Eintracht from Freiburg last month.

The match was decided only in the closing minutes.

Bayer Leverkusen took the lead, went behind, and found the equalizer shortly before stoppage time in the second half.

Hoffenheim had lost from winning positions in the first two Bundesliga rounds this season.

This Saturday, the team went in front and then conceded the equalizer.

But just as fears of a third comeback defeat started to grow, Hoffenheim regained the lead and left the pitch with all three points.

articles.summary: Gran puesta en escena del ex del Real Madrid para frenar en Anfield a los de Iraola
articles.body: Álvaro Arbeloa respira (más) tranquilo. El ex del Real Madrid volvía a Anfield y 'su' Fulham consiguió arrebatarle un empate al Liverpool (0-0) para conquistar su primer punto -marcha 17º- en esta Premier. Los de Andoni Iraola, por su parte, marchan sextos con seis unidades. Empezó el partido con un disparo cruzado de Isak en el 9' tras un pase filtrado por Barcola. Fue un espejismo. Acto seguido, en el 11', un fallo en salida de Alisson derivó en un tiro de Gonzalo García que salvó Jacquet bajo palos. El 'Pool', hasta el descanso, apenas consiguió inquietar al Fulham con un cabezazo de Víctor Muñoz a la salida de un córner botado por Szoboszlai que desviaron al alimón entre Leno y el larguero. A destacar la personalidad y la puesta en escena de los de Arbeloa, que, sin gozar de grandísimas ocasiones, llegaron a acumular tramos de hasta un 73% de posesión en Anfield. Los de Iraola no encontraron la manera de 'meter mano' al Fulham en el debut de Affengruber, ex del Elche. A destacar, apenas, una jugada personal de Isak (52') y un tiro de Szoboszlai (67'). Ambos acabaron en las manos de Leno. La entrada de Kerkez (46'), Gakpo (60'), Mac Allister (60'), Frimpong (72') y Ngumoha (72') no mejoró al 'Pool'. Los de Arbeloa, cómodos, probaron suerte con un tiro de King desde la frontal en el 76' que desvió Alisson a córner y un disparo de Kevin en el 79', ya sin Gonzalo sobre el 'verde', que salió desviado. La última 'bala' fue un córner de Szoboszlai que cabeceó desviado Isak en el 92'. Ngumoha, ya en el 94' envió a las nubes un centro de Frimpong. Arbeloa respira... a costa de Iraola.

articles.title: Dos zarpazos de Roberto tumban a Osasuna
articles.standfirst: El delantero castigó los errores defensivos del conjunto navarro
articles.summary: El delantero castigó los errores defensivos del conjunto navarro
articles.body: Roberto Fernández tumbó a Osasuna en dos zarpazos. El delantero del Espanyol, que está entre los máximos goleadores del campeonato, se aprovechó la desconexión defensiva de la zaga rojilla para dar tres puntos de oro a su equipo. Los navarros, por su parte, dejan una imagen preocupante. El Espanyol entró mucho mejor que Osasuna al partido y solo necesitó tres minutos para asestar el primer golpe. Una jugada que se inició en Dmitrovic y que El Hilali, Marcos y Roberto se encargaron de finalizar. Cuatro pases para que el delantero del Espanyol aprovechase el despiste de Rockson en la marca para batir a Sergio Herrera. La tarde iba de despistes. A los 17 minutos Roberto volvía a marcar aprovechando un error grosero de Catena que, incomprensiblemente, dejó pasar un centro lateral en vez de despejar y el 9 espanyolista no desaprovechó el regalo. El respetable estaba de uñas con el equipo por la pobre propuesta futbolística que estaba ofreciendo Osasuna, pero estaba aún más cabreado con la labor del colegiado balear Luis Bestard que, con 0-1 en el marcador, se comió un penalti claro de Riedel sobre Raúl García, sin que el VAR considerase oportuno intervenir. Además, mostró un criterio desconcertante con las tarjetas amarillas. El conjunto navarro tuvo pocas cosas positivas que destacar en la primera parte. Tan solo la rapidez y el desborde de Kike Barja por banda izquierda y el trabajo infatigable de Ante Budimir. Precisamente, el croata tuvo la ocasión más clara de su equipo en la primera parte con un cabezazo a servicio de Barja que se marchó alto. Esta acción y el gol anulado a Rubén García porque el balón había traspasado la línea de fondo antes de que Kike Barja pudiese poner el balón en las botas de su compañero fueron las únicas ocasiones destacables de Osasuna antes del descanso. Tras el descanso, Ramis reaccionó dando entrada en el campo a Abel Bretones en sustitución de Rico, que había pasado completamente desapercibido. Pero nada se arregló en Osasuna más allá de un inicial disparo lejano de Rubén García que blocó bien Dmitrovic. Los errores en defensa seguían sucediéndose. El de Rockson estuvo a punto de costarle el 0-3 a los rojillos si no llega a ser por la rápida intervención de Sergio Herrera. El Espanyol tenía el partido controlado y se dedicaba a contemporizar y esperar a que pasasen los minutos, aunque sin renunciar al ataque, como en una jugada en la que Roberto se quejaba de un posible penalti por un pisotón del que el colegiado no quiso saber nada. Los cambios introducidos durante la segunda parte dieron un impulso a Osasuna en el último cuarto de hora. Raúl Moro era una amenaza por la banda izquierda y generó acciones de peligro que no se pudieron concretar. Osasuna necesita mejorar con urgencia.

articles.title: El Chelsea de Xabi Alonso 'patina' con el Hull
articles.standfirst: El recién ascendido rescató un punto ante los 'blues', que venían de caer con el Arsenal
articles.summary: El recién ascendido rescató un punto ante los 'blues', que venían de caer con el Arsenal
articles.body: El Chelsea de Xabi Alonso necesita mejorar. Ganaron sus dos primeros partidos de Premier, pero, tras caer con el Arsenal (2-1), han vuelto a tropezar, esta vez en casa contra el recién ascendido Hull City (2-2), que continúa invicto. El empate deja cuarto a los de Xabi Alonso con siete puntos, uno menos que el propio Hull, que es tercero. Es curioso. Morgan Rogers puso en ventaja a los 'blues' nada más empezar, en el 7'. Palmer conectó para Joao Pedro y éste abrió hacia la izquierda para el ex del Aston Villa, que sorprendió a Tzolakis, con un potente zurdazo al palo corto. Ha caído de pie el internacional inglés en el Bridge: suma siete contribuciones de gol en seis partidos. No sólo eso. Puso fin, 277 minutos después, a la imbatibilidad de Tzolakis: el Hull City era el único equipo que aún no había encajado goles en la Premier League. Los 'tigres', recién ascendidos, le dieron la vuelta al partido en 6'. Sacó en largo Tzolakis, Hato se comió el centro de Ryan Giles y Mohamed Belloumi al empaló a la red con la zurda en el 28'. Colwill evitó el 2-2 en el 32' al desviar un disparo de Coyle. De poco sirvió. Acto seguido, a la salida de un córner, Ajayi cabeceó al larguero aprovechando la mala salida de 'El Dibu' Martínez y el propio Belloumi marcó con un tiro desde la frontal tras una dejada de McBurnie. Desde Oumar Niasse (2017) no hacía doblete un jugador del Hull en la Premier. El Chelsea, por su parte, necesita mejorar, sobre todo, atrás. Ya son 20 partidos de Liga encajando, al menos, un gol. No le sucedía desde hacía 65 años. Pudo ser peor. Al 'Dibu' se le escapó un tiro desde fuera del área de Slater en el 61', pero el meta argentino se rehizo para salvar el mano a mano con McBurnie. El Chelsea, empeñado en buscar centros laterales, igualó en el 66' por medio de Joao Pedro. El 'MVP' de la Premier en agosto apareció para rematar con la zurda un pase atrás de Cole Palmer. Tres goles y dos asistencias acumula ya en Liga el brasileño. El tramo final del partido sirvió para agrandar la figura de Tzolakis. El exportero de Olympiacos atrapó un tiro de James desde la frontal en el 76', salvó un mano a mano con Joao Pedro en el 84' y un tiro sin apenas ángulo de Estevao en el 92'. También tuvo sus opciones el Hull, que continúa invicto para ganar. El 'Dibu' Martínez salvó en el 87' un remate en boca de gol de Mohamed-Ali Cho tras un centro de Giles desde la izquierda. El Chelsea de Xabi Alonso aún está en construcción.

articles.title: El Aston Villa de Emery continúa sin ganar y es penúltimo
articles.standfirst: Los goles de Liam Delap e Igor Jesus derrotaron a los 'villanos' en casa
articles.summary: Los goles de Liam Delap e Igor Jesus derrotaron a los 'villanos' en casa
articles.body: La victoria en Champions League fue un espejismo para Unai Emery. De vuelta a la Premier League, de vuelta a las andadas. Su Aston Villa perdió contra el Nottingham Forest y el balance tras cuatro jornadas es de tres derrotas, un empate y un solo gol a favor. Los 'Villanos', penúltimos, deberían haber empezado ganando en los cinco primeros minutos, pero Mats Selz, con una doble parada espectacular, evitó el 1-0 y a partir de ahí se desencadenó la derrota de los de Birmingham. Nada más salir del descanso, Liam Delap atrapó una pelota en la frontal regateó a un jugador y con un disparo con la zurda batió a Suzuki. Al Villa le costó 20 minutos recuperarse y a quince del final, Alysson, con un cabezazo en el primer palo, igualó el encuentro con el primer gol liguero de los de Emery esta temporada. El empate no era bueno, obviamente, pero era mejor que una nueva derrota en casa. Sin embargo, en el minuto 88, una gran combinación de los de Oliver Glasner por banda derecha, comandada por Daniel Muñoz, acabó con Morgan Gibbs-White asistiendo a Igor Jesús y el brasileño mandando los tres puntos Nottingham. Después de cuatro jornadas, el Aston Villa es penúltimo, con un solo punto, un solo gol a favor y siete en contra. Si el Conventry City puntúa esta jornada, los de Emery acabarán el fin de semana como colistas de la competición. El Forest, por su parte, logra la primera victoria de la temporada y es undécimo, con cinco unidades.

articles.title: Bryce Underwood's Struggles Analyzed by CFB Insiders, Michigan QB 'Looks Like He's Seeing Ghosts'
articles.summary: Ahead of Saturday's game between No. 11 Oklahoma and unranked Michigan, an anonymous coach suggested that the Sooners created the blueprint for stopping Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood last season.
articles.body:
Ahead of Saturday's game between No. 11 Oklahoma and unranked Michigan, an anonymous coach suggested that the Sooners created the blueprint for stopping Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood last season.

In 2025, Oklahoma beat Michigan 24-13, and Underwood was held to just 142 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions on 9-of-24 passing.

Speaking to Bruce Feldman of The Athletic, a Big Ten defensive coach said, "Oklahoma put a lot of stuff on tape [to defend Underwood] for the playbook last year. [Sooners coach Brent] Venables exposed him. Underwood struggles with all that variance that Venables loves to do. They have so much volume of stuff, and guys are getting calls in late. It's almost like OU can be too exotic with all they're doing, but even if they cut [a Michigan receiver] loose, I don't know if Underwood could find him. It looks like he's seeing ghosts. This is not a great matchup for him."

Michigan landed Underwood, who was the No. 1 overall player in 247Sports ' class of 2025 rankings, thanks to a reported $12.5 million NIL deal .

Expectations were high for Underwood as a freshman last season, but he largely struggled as a passer, completing 60.3 percent of his attempts for 2,428 yards, 11 touchdowns and nine interceptions.

His 2026 campaign didn't get off to a much better start, as he went 12-of-22 for 170 yards with one touchdown and one interception in a controversial 13-12 win over Western Michigan.

Underwood threw a game-winning, Hail Mary touchdown to JJ Buchanan as time expired, but that was only because the officials put one second back on the clock after the first Hail Mary was incomplete.

The 19-year-old Underwood has yet to come anywhere close to living up to his billing, and if he has another rough outing against the Sooners, it is fair to wonder how long head coach Kyle Whittingham will be willing to stick with him as the QB1.

articles.title: Chelsea draw with Hull, Liverpool held by Fulham and Villa remain winless
articles.summary: Hull nearly claim Premier League win at Chelsea, while Liverpool and Fulham fire blanks and Aston Villa lose again.
articles.body:
Hull held free-scoring Chelsea to a 2-2 draw at Stamford Bridge to go third in the Premier League on Saturday as Liverpool failed to find a way past struggling Fulham in a 0-0 draw.

It was a familiar tale for Chelsea as the front three of Morgan Rogers, Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer dazzled, but the Blues were undone by their inability to defend.

In five games against top-flight opposition since Xabi Alonso took charge, Chelsea have scored 16 times and conceded 12.

Hull were the last side in the Premier League to concede, but after three clean sheets, they were finally breached when Rogers drilled in at the near post on seven minutes.

Mohamed Belloumi took advantage of Chelsea’s slackness at the back to blast home on the volley after Jorrel Hato got caught under a cross to the back post.

The Algerian winger then put Hull in front with a deflected strike after Emi Martinez failed to deal with a corner.

Pedro drilled a Palmer cross into the top corner to bring Chelsea level just after the hour mark.

But the home side could not find a winner as Hull’s honeymoon back in the Premier League goes on, with only defending champions Arsenal and Manchester City above them in the table.

Liverpool held as Fulham fight for former Real Madrid boss

Liverpool remain unbeaten under Andoni Iraola, but there were boos at Anfield after Fulham picked up their first point under Alvaro Arbeloa.

Former Liverpool defender Arbeloa was reportedly fighting for his job after losing his first three league matches since arriving in west London from Real Madrid.

Yet a Liverpool forward line featuring three 100 million pounds ($135m) players in Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak failed to click against the Cottagers’ leaky defence.

Indeed, it was Fulham who had the better chances to take all three points as Gonzalo Garcia missed a glorious opportunity in the first half and Alisson Becker produced a brilliant save to deny Josh King the winner.

Liverpool climb to sixth but could find themselves already six points off the top should Arsenal win at Sunderland later on Saturday.

Aston Villa are rooted in the relegation zone after Nottingham Forest exacted revenge with a 2-1 win at Villa Park.

Villa beat their Midlands rivals in the Europa League semifinals last season on their way to lifting a first trophy in 30 years.

Many eyebrows were raised at the reported 45 million pounds ($61m) club record Forest paid Chelsea for Liam Delap after failing to make the grade at Stamford Bridge.

But the striker proved his worth with a long-range shot into the bottom corner to open the scoring.

Alysson levelled with Villa’s first league goal of the season, but Igor Jesus secured Oliver Glasner’s first win as Forest boss.

His old club Crystal Palace’s poor start to the campaign continued with a 3-2 home defeat to Ipswich.

The visitors were aided by Axel Disasi’s first half red card as Zian Flemming’s first goal for the Tractor Boys snatched all three points in stoppage time.

Brentford remain unbeaten, thanks to Kevin Schade’s double in a 2-2 draw at Bournemouth.

The Cherries, by contrast, are yet to win in the Premier League under Marco Rose, despite leading in all four games.

Tottenham are aiming to kick-start their league season with a first goal and win at home to Everton later.

Manchester United host local rivals City in the pick of Sunday’s action.

articles.title: Chelsea 2-2 Hull City: Tigers remain unbeaten as poor Blues defending leads to enthralling draw
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Chelsea draw 2-2 with Hull City in the Premier League; the visitors couldn’t contain the attacking trio of Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro; poor defending from Chelsea let Mohamed Belloumi score twice to earn a point
articles.body:
Sergej Jakirovic joked pre-match that the only way to stop Xabi Alonso's potent attack was to kick them. While they were unable to do that, they made the most of some calamitous moments at the back to leave west London with a point.

The hosts made the perfect start as a rapid counter-attack from a Hull corner ended with Morgan Rogers firing past Konstantinos Tzolakis at his near post.

It was no more than Chelsea deserved after a positive start, but that was quickly undone. First, Jorrel Hato let the ball bounce over him inside his own penalty area, inviting Mohamed Belloumi to pounce and find the equaliser.

Belloumi was on hand to complete the turnaround moments later - putting Hull momentarily top of the league - as his strike from the edge of the box deflected off Levi Colwill and beat Emi Martinez.

It should have been three as a spilled effort fell to Oli McBurnie, only for Martinez to make up with a remarkable stop from close range. It proved to be a costly miss as Cole Palmer found Joao Pedro before the Brazilian smashed an equaliser into the roof of the net just after the hour mark.

Both sides had golden chances to win it, with Rogers and Mohamed-Ali Cho striking straight at the respective goalkeepers when goals seemed inevitable. However, it's was all smiles for Jakirovic and Hull, who came away from their toughest test of the season with plenty to be proud of.

7: GOAL! Hull’s defence breached for the first time as Rogers gives Chelsea the lead.

22: SAVE! Tzolakis called into action to deny Neto.

28: GOAL! Awful Hato defending allows Belloumi to equalise.

33: CLOSE! Coyle squanders glorious chance thanks to Colwill block.

34: GOAL! From the resulting corner, Belloumi’s strike deflects off Colwill and beats Martinez.

53: POST! Tzolakis’ fingertips pushes stunning James free-kick onto the post.

61: SAVE! Martinez recovers after initial spill to make incredible stop to deny McBurnie.

66: GOAL! Joao Pedro finds the roof of the net from close range.

84: SAVE! Rogers squanders big chance to give hosts lead.

87: SAVE! Cho misses huge chance from six yards out as Martinez thwarts substitute

"Maybe entertaining, but I hope one day you'll say it was a boring game and we win and we don't give these entertaining moments," said Alonso, whose team have now let in 12 goals in his six matches in charge.

"It kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to fix them. When we get the lead, you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially for the first goal. We can do much better. It was too soft.

"That momentum that we had [was lost], it changed the mood. It's something we need to keep talking and address. We will get better, but it's having an impact on our performances.

"Overall I think that we are attacking better than defending. It's a big topic and a big theme for us. It's just four [league] games, but the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don't like it.

"We can do better for sure. When we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distances. I'm sure that we can do better."

"I feel good. We have to be happy. It's a huge result for us.

"We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie, but Martinez's save was excellent. We had an excellent chance for [Mohamed-Al] Cho [near the end], Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

"We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match."

Attack vs defence - Alonso needs to focus on the latter

Much of the talk surrounding the Chelsea team that Xabi Alonso is in the midst of creating is what they are capable of in attack. How can you stop JP Morgan?

No one has been able to stop them from contributing at least one goal per game this season, but you can't bank on them to get you out of footballing bankruptcy if you can't keep clean sheets.

It is a problem that has impacted the Blues for some time, not just under Alonso. This is the 20th Premier League game in a row their defence has been breached.

The signing of a World Cup winner and multi-time Yashin trophy winner in the form of Emi Martinez is all well and good. However, if he has defenders not doing the basics in front of him, he may as well be Robert Sanchez.

The 1.32 xG that Hull managed was a fair reflection of how dangerous they were at times at Stamford Bridge. And it wasn't like they carved open the hosts. Most of the time, they had chances put on a plate.

The potential in attack is obvious, and certainly exciting. However, Alonso needs to tap into his learnings under Jose Mourinho and make this Chelsea side much tougher to score against if he wants to challenge.

Aaron Collins put MK Dons ahead, only for Peterborough's Chris Conn-Clarke to equalise late on.

The stalemate means the Dons are still yet to win a league game this season, while Posh only have one win to their name so far.

Bass would also make a fingertrip save to deny Collins' cross-shot after half-time before Crowley blazed over from a good position.

articles.title: Aston Villa 1-2 Nottingham Forest: Oliver Glasner masterminds another win over Unai Emery
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Aston Villa remain without a league win this season; Oliver Glasner got his first victory as Nottingham Forest boss with Igor Jesus netting a late winner
articles.body:
Once again, Oliver Glasner got the better of Emery, who remains winless in eight matches against the Austrian.

Liam Delap went some way to paying back his £50m fee as he fired Forest in front after just 45 seconds of the second half.

Villa needed inspiration and Emery turned to his new signings Johan Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye. The changes injected much-needed energy into the hosts and they were rewarded when Alysson struck his first goal for the club to level.

At that point, momentum appeared to be swinging Villa's way.

However, with 10 minutes remaining, Ian Maatsen was forced off after hobbling badly. Villa had already used all their substitutes, leaving them with 10 men for the closing stages.

Forest sensed an opportunity and they took it.

With just two minutes remaining, Igor Jesus found the decisive finish to send the travelling Forest supporters wild.

Emery is having to rebuild following a turbulent summer, where a host of key players were sold, but progress is slow. The result leaves Villa with just one point from their first four games and in the bottom three.

9: HOW DID VILLA NOT SCORE!? Victor Lindelof is somehow denied by the post and a goal-line save from Mats Sels.

45: BIG CHANCE FOR FOREST! The away side wait for their moment and hit on the break but Neco Williams blazes over after a brilliant pass from James McAtee.

46: GOAL! With their first attack after the break, Forest take the lead as Delap thumps one home from 25 yards.

59: CHANCE FOR NDOYE! Forest keep the pressure on but can't find a second goal with Dan Ndoye being denied by a goal-saving block from Tyrone Mings.

64: SUBS! Emery introduces Manzambi and Mbaye from the bench to spark Villa into life.

73: GOAL! McGinn provides the quality from the win and Alysson flicks home a neat header.

80: INJURY! With the game in the balance, McAtee's challenge on Maatsen leaves him unable to continue and Villa had already made all their changes.

88: GOAL! Forest sense their opportunity and a wonderful move down the right ends with Gibbs-White flicking one to Jesus who rolls home the winner.

Emery fumes over McAtee tackle on Maatsen: 'It's a red card'

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery speaking to Sky Sports said:

"We played the first half like we planned, we dominate, we didn't concede so much. We didn't score, but we were playing in the way we wanted. The second half, completely different. I don't know why, but we started so poor. They scored and they were creating chances.

"We corrected it and in that moment maybe we should keep the same way we were, but we couldn't. And the injury of Ian Maatsen was a key moment because the tackle was strong. And we were finishing the last 15 minutes with one player less for one tackle and they were playing with 11. For me, VAR should be there. I think it's a red card.

"If I was in the VAR and I was a referee, it was a red card."

Glasner remaining humble despite unbeaten Emery record

Oliver Glasner speaking about his record over Emery:

"I spoke to him before the game, and it's still 5-2 for him, five European trophies to two. So I said to myself, 'Oliver Glasner, stay humble'.

"And this is how I will stay. Every win is great, but I didn't play one second today. The players deserve all the credit because they did so well. And our fans deserve the credit because they supported us."

They had the clearer chances in the second half too, Josh King forcing Alisson to tip the ball wide before Rodrigo Muniz should have finished when fed by fellow substitute Kevin as Fulham pushed for an unlikely winner. Alexander Isak glanced wide at the other end in stoppage time.

The result means that Andoni Iraola is still searching for his first Premier League win at Anfield and has now drawn three of his first four games in the competition as Liverpool boss. Unbeaten but unsatisfied. The positives here all belonged to the ex-Red Arbeloa.

22 - CROSSBAR! Munoz heads Tsimikas' corner against the bar

76 - SAVE ! King tries a shot from distance but Alisson tips over

79 - MISS! Kevin crosses but Muniz fails to control when through

90+1 - WIDE! Isak glances header wide from Szoboszlai's corner

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola speaking in the press conference:

"In the end, this is the easier one for me, for you, for everyone - our players were tired. I think there is a lack of freshness, definitely. We cannot hide it.

"I think it's the worst turnaround in terms of 60-something hours between the games, after a very big game the other day. But this is going to happen more times, maybe with one more day, maybe. But sometimes it's going to happen the same way during the season.

"We have to adapt to these circumstances. It's this kind of game that you need to win, sometimes with a set play, sometimes with a shot from the edge, sometimes from a moment of brilliance from the offensive players and we haven't had that today. We've been clearly not as good offensively as we've been in other days."

"I think today, especially in the first half, we were arriving late to the presses. It's clear. I think we improved this part a lot in the second half. I think we've been better structured, I think we controlled better the game in the second half, even without scoring the goal."

"I didn't feel it three days ago against Atletico Madrid. Is it because we haven't won? I don't know. I prefer to play at home, definitely I prefer to play at home. We cannot find the reasons outside, we have to find the reasons inside the pitch."

Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa speaking in the press conference:

"I know that when you are not winning games, it's not so easy that your players believe in your ideas. I know everything is easy when you win but they believe in the way that we have been working and I showed them the things that we were doing so well.

"I think there were so many things that we did well but we have been making mistakes and of course, in this league, if you make mistakes, they will punish you. That's the league, that's the level and we need to understand that, how important it is.

"If you have chances, try to take those chances but also to be a little bit more balanced and control the transition against a team when all teams here in England have quick players. I think we did better and we realised how important it is to be balanced.

"From my first day, we trained so hard about the transition. But I think everything changed after the Crystal Palace game because I think we have been working all this week, but in the first week also, how important it is to be balanced when you have the ball."

Analysis: Did Atletico impact Iraola's Liverpool?

There were celebrations at Anfield on Wednesday evening when Andoni Iraola picked up the first Champions League win of his coaching career against Atletico Madrid. But that win was always going to come at some point this season. There was a bigger question.

One of the themes of this Liverpool season was always likely to be how the Basque coach would be able to cope with an increased schedule, having impressed at Rayo Vallecano and Bournemouth without the added challenge of European commitments.

This was the first test of that and Liverpool did not pass it. They were unable to play at the tempo that Iraola usually demands, starting slowly and struggling to raise the level. Fulham, with an injection of attacking substitutes of their own, looked as likely to win it.

Iraola's unbeaten run as Liverpool boss continues, one that extends back to the first week of January for him personally given his exploits with the Cherries. But home games against Nottingham Forest and Fulham have yielded only two points. More is needed.

articles.body: El Málaga CF completó este sábado por la mañana en La Rosaleda la última sesión de trabajo antes de poner rumbo a Vigo. El conjunto blanquiazul ya tiene todo preparado para medirse este domingo al Celta en Balaídos, en el encuentro correspondiente a la quinta jornada de LaLiga EA Sports. La sesión arrancó con una charla técnica de Funes, antes de dar paso al trabajo de activación física, los rondos y diferentes partidillos. El entrenamiento también tuvo su espacio para las acciones de estrategia, en una jornada que dejó dos nuevas bajas. Aznou y Álex Pastor no pudieron ejercitarse con normalidad debido a un virus gastrointestinal. La parte positiva estuvo en la presencia de Eneko y Adrián Niño, que ya están disponibles para el técnico lojeño. De hecho, Funes podrá contar por primera vez esta temporada con sus tres delanteros centros, una alternativa más para el ataque de cara al duelo de Balaídos. Aznou y Álex Pastor se suman a una lista de ausencias en la que ya estaban Lobete y Aarón Ochoa, ambos por lesiones de larga duración. Tampoco estarán Fernando Calero y Murillo, que continúan con sus respectivos procesos de recuperación. A ellos se une Haitam, que sigue apartado por sus problemas de índole personal. El Málaga viajará esta tarde hasta Pontevedra, donde hará noche antes de desplazarse este domingo a Vigo. El encuentro ante el Celta está fijado para las 14:00 horas en Balaídos. Funes afronta así su primer desplazamiento liguero fuera de casa con nuevas bajas, aunque recupera efectivos importantes para el frente ofensivo. Porteros: Alfonso Herrero y Carlos López. articles.title: Texas Sen. Ted Cruz booed in Austin while trying to promote Protect College Sports Act on 'College GameDay'
articles.summary: The PCSA is set to be voted on by the Senate next week.
articles.body:
Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) did not get much crowd support during his appearance on ESPN's "College GameDay" on Saturday.

Cruz did a live interview with the pregame show in Austin to promote the Protect College Sports Act ahead of No. 1 Ohio State's visit to No. 4 Texas . Cruz, who is a co-sponsor of the bill for federal legislation to govern college sports, was met with boos as he tried to advocate for the Senate bill. "Ted, you suck" chants even emanated from the crowd.

This was the second week in a row that "College GameDay" had a segment in support of the Protect College Sports Act. Last week, it was a conversation between hosts Nick Saban and Pat McAfee.

Cruz said the Senate is expected to vote on the bill this week after a summer vote had been delayed past the Senate's August recess. The bill needs 60 votes to pass the Senate, and then needs to pass the House and be signed by President Donald Trump to go into law. Trump has signaled his support for the bill and is expected to sign off if the bill gets through both chambers.

Though the bill has bipartisan support — Cruz's co-sponsor is Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.) — it is not without its detractors. Sen. Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) has been one of the most outspoken senators against the bill. Murphy even engaged in a social media back-and-forth with Texas Tech board of regents president Cody Campbell over the bill earlier in the week.

Campbell is funding television ads supporting the bill , and those ads have included Saban and Colorado coach Deion Sanders.

Cruz said in his appearance Saturday that his confidence in the bill passing the Senate was "very, very high."

The college sports landscape has drastically changed since the creation of the NIL initiative. When it was created, it was intended to compensate players for their autographs or to include them in an annual video game, but it has become a yearly bidding war for both recruits and transfers.

The PCSA itself is 230 pages long . Rather than going through the entire bill, the Congress website offers a summary.

"This bill establishes requirements for name, image, or likeness (NIL) agreements for college student athletes and provides a limited antitrust exemption for schools and conferences to pool and sell certain college sports media rights. The requirements address elements of the court-approved agreement to settle In re College Athlete NIL Litigation (i.e., House settlement ). First, the bill statutorily prohibits institutions, conferences, or interstate intercollegiate athletic associations (e.g., the National Collegiate Athletic Association [NCAA]) from restricting student athletes from entering NIL agreements (subject to specified limitations). Students must report to their institution NIL compensation greater than $600. The bill requires agents to register with a state and caps agent endorsement contract fees at 5%. The bill also provides student athletes with one transfer without losing athletic eligibility and restricts football personnel from becoming the head football coach at a different institution during the same season. Further, the bill prohibits institutions, conferences, or specified entities acting for the benefit of an institution from providing athletes with compensation that circumvents the limit on sharing revenue with student athletes established under the House settlement. The bill also makes the limit permanent and provides for an annual inflation adjustment. Additionally, the bill establishes (subject to specified conditions) a limited antitrust exemption for institutions or conferences that form joint agreements to transfer their sports telecasting rights to a third party. Such an agreement requires participation from at least 75% of the institutions in the Football Bowl Subdivision."

The requirements address elements of the court-approved agreement to settle In re College Athlete NIL Litigation (i.e., House settlement ).

On the one hand, college sports fans will be intrigued by the inclusion of new rules regarding transfers and coaches leaving for other programs.

On the other, there is assuredly plenty of details and information about the NIL compensation — what is capped and what is allowed. One of the main opposing viewpoints of the bill is that it includes legislation that would limit how much players can earn, but not coaches or schools who benefit from them.

This intersection of sports and politics may continue, and in a big way. In a previous appearance discussing the bill, Cruz mentioned that if it passes, President Trump would sign it into law on an episode of "College GameDay."

articles.title: Crystal Palace 2-3 Ipswich Town: Zian Flemming's strike earns Tractor Boys win at Selhurst Park
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Premier League match between Crystal Palace and Ipswich at Selhurst Park; goals from Emersonn, Leif Davis and Zian Flemming seal a comeback victory for Gary O'Neil's men
articles.body:
Goals from Emersonn and Leif Davis answered Anan Khalaili's opener, before substitute Zian Flemming struck the 90th-minute winner after Jorgen Strand Larsen had pulled the Eagles level.

That goal ended a run of 32 Premier League games - stretching back to December 2001 - in which the Tractor Boys had conceded first and failed to win.

Latest news and rumours: Crystal Palace | Ipswich

Having beaten Fulham and Middlesbrough in their last two outings, Palace were looking to make it a perfect week - and chances of that happening increased when Anan Khalaili collected Daichi Kamada's square ball, took one touch and struck a sweet shot, which took a slight deflection off Ipswich full-back Davis on its way past Kjell Scherpen.

As the hosts sought out a second, Strand Larsen saw a cracking volley batted away. But, before long, they were pegged back instead.

Davis hit a cross from the left and, seemingly convinced he had been offside when he collected the ball, Palace switched off, which allowed Emersonn to find the net with a header under no pressure.

Ipswich received a major boost when Axel Disasi was shown a straight red card 34 minutes in after catching Jack Clarke on the shin with his studs - and they took advantage by establishing the lead on the stroke of half-time when Davis scored a free header.

Palace started to up the tempo with around 20 minutes to go, with Quiten Timber guilty of passing up two opportunities to equalise, and the noise was deafening when Strand Larsen held off his man to fire into the bottom-left corner and level.

But their efforts were rendered useless in the 90th minute when Flemming reacted quickest when a looping header from Davis came back off the crossbar and stylishly tucked in the winner.

14: GOAL ! Anan Khalali hits a sweet shot from the edge of the box, which goes in with a deflection off the leg of an Ipswich player.

18: CHANCE ! Jorgen Strand Larsen's volley is batted away by Scherpen, before his follow-up is blocked.

23: GOAL ! Ipswich level with their first shot of the game, as Leif Davis' cross is headed in by Emersonn.

34: RED CARD ! Palace defender Axel Disasi is shown a straight red card for catching Jack Clarke on the shin with his studs.

45: GOAL ! Ipswich take the lead for the first time as Davis plants a free header past Walter Benitez.

75: GOAL ! Daichi Kamada feeds Strand Larsen, who holds off Issa Diop and fires into the bottom-left corner.

90: GOAL ! A looping header comes back off the crossbar, and Ipswich substitute Zian Flemming bundles in the winner.

Sage 'frustrated' by third league defeat

"We are really frustrated because of the context of the game. We were ahead before conceding the 1-1 goal from their first opportunity, and the red card forced me to reorganise the team into a 5-3-1 while keeping many of our principles.

"But we made a tactical mistake at the end of the first half and they scored the second goal.

"The second half, we came back with the same organisation, we created things, we had the ball, we came to 2-2 and had the opportunity to make it 3-2, missed it. And, at the end, it's very hard to concede the third goal in the same way, with a cross and a ball we didn't win into our box.

"I'm really frustrated for the players because they gave a lot on the pitch and they don't have the result for their efforts."

On Jaydee Canvot's omission: "This was a sporting decision, but I have to be honest, I didn't take him in the team because of his game against Fulham and what he did during the week.

"I spoke with him. I need more from him.

"I'm sure he is able to do it and I wait for a good reaction on his part from Monday."

O'Neil: It wasn't perfect, but winning away is tough

"I'm pleased. Winning away in the Premier League is tough, (especially) against teams playing in Europe this season. Really pleased to have two wins on the board after four matches. It's a big plus for us.

"I'm really pleased with the group, what they gave; lots of emotion, lots of having to respond to set-backs, respond to positives. It wasn't perfect, but we won. We found a way to win, we deserved to win as well, which is important.

"We happily take the three points and send the fans back up the A12 happy and get ready for a big week, with Arsenal and Everton coming next."

On Emersonn : "I thought he was excellent today - I'd hate to play against him! He bashes people around, he runs in behind, he looks after the ball, he's a threat. Really pleased with how quickly he's taken to the league.

"The coaching staff work really hard with him on his technical stuff because it was a problem for him before and he's getting better very, very quickly.

"I thought it was another excellent No 9 performance from him today."

Hull not the only newly-promoted team going well

Analysis by Sky Sports' Dan Long at Selhurst Park:

When they first returned to the Premier League in 2024/25, it was 16 games before Ipswich had recorded two wins.

This time around, it has taken just four.

They beat Sunderland on the opening day, took the lead against Man Utd at Old Trafford the following week - before an eventual 5-2 defeat - and recorded a higher xG than Liverpool in the 2-0 loss last time out.

And against Crystal Palace, both Emersonn and Leif Davis' headers were all too easy. Axel Disasi's sending off gave them an extra boost, but they took advantage when opportunities presented themselves.

When Palace's equaliser made it 2-2, they did not go all out, desperate for the winner; they just waited, exercising patience, with the belief the winner would come, which it eventually did.

While taking three points at Selhurst Park was impressive, equally - if not more so - was the fact it was the third time in the four games they have played that they have conceded less than 0.70 xG.

Fellow newly-promoted side Hull are taking all the plaudits for their start on their return to the Premier League, and rightly so - but, out of the spotlight, Ipswich are going well, too.

articles.title: Southampton 4-1 Bristol City: Cyle Larin scores twice in Saints win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Southampton and Bristol City at St Mary's on Saturday; Cyle Larin's double, Kuryu Matsuki and Finn Azaz seal a comfortable win for the Saints.
articles.body:
Larin scored in either half, with late goals from Kuryu Matsuki and Finn Azaz after Lorent Tolaj had pulled one back for visitors City.

The Saints are formidable opposition at St Mary's and have not lost on their own patch since January but recent results against the Robins had not gone in their favour.

They had won just one of the last eight meetings between the two.

Michael Skubala's Robins had already scored five set-piece goals and came close to another as early as the second minute when Tolaj latched on to a loose ball from a free-kick but could not beat Daniel Peretz.

Five minutes later, City captain Jason Knight forced Peretz into a fine save following a corner after Larin's headed clearance had fallen to him on the edge of the penalty area.

The away side were dominating the early stages and former Saint Dom Ballard almost scored after latching onto a long ball from Joe Williams and lobbing it over Peretz, only for Keven Schlotterbeck to clear acrobatically off the line.

Unlike Southampton, City had not had a midweek fixture and were looking the fresher of the two sides.

But Saints had their first chance on 19 minutes when Larin failed to convert James Bree's low cross from close range.

In the next minute, a surging run from Leo Scienza set up a chance for Matsuki to shoot but Sam Tickle was able to beat away his fierce effort at the near post.

With Saints a man down after Scienza had limped off for treatment following a clash with George Tanner, Tonda Eckert's men took an unlikely lead.

Azaz wriggled through a gap to find Larin and the Canadian superbly glided past two challenges before curling deftly into the top right corner.

City continued to pose problems and their final chance of the half came when Rio Cardines crossed to Ballard but the forward directed his header just past the far post.

Free-scoring Larin got Saints the goal they desperately needed on the hour mark when he pounced on a loose ball after Tanner had blocked James Ward-Prowse's initial effort, following brilliant work from Scienza.

City pulled one back five minutes later when Nathan Wood's headed clearance dropped to Cardines and he volleyed back into the area with Tolaj diverting it low into the corner.

The subsequent nervy spell around St Mary's ended when Matsuki fired a superb effort into the bottom right-hand corner following another clever pass from Azaz.

Azaz then got the goal his performance deserved, slotting past Tickle after being teed up by Divin Mubama.

"It wasn't an easy start to the game and then I've decided at half-time that it's probably not the day where we can go after them.

"Sometimes you have to accept maybe you have to defend a little bit more, that you don't touch the ball as often. And then you need to use those moments when you go forward. I think the win today belongs to the players, because they have left everything on the pitch.

"It just comes down to the mindset you have, to the togetherness as a group, how you grind out those games, especially if it's been a long block now, physically and mentally.

"I think you could just see from the very first minute today that there was a team on the pitch that played midweek against Swansea and had to run a lot, the most that we've had to run all season, and a team on the pitch that had a whole week to prepare."

"The scoreline overshadows it and probably flatters them a little bit. I thought we more than matched them in the first half and were the better team.

"I was looking at the game, at their goal. We created chances and to come here and I think we should have scored two at least.

"But that's football. The back end of the game where we opened up too much was the frustrating bit because the scoreline frustrates us. But when we look at that performance, and I will, I think it'll probably be a good performance."

articles.title: Preston North End 0-1 Lincoln City: Freddie Draper scores late Imps winner
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Preston North End and Lincoln City at Deepdale on Saturday; Freddie Draper scores late winner as the Imps seal a narrow win at struggling Lilywhites.
articles.body:
The first half ended goalless with the hosts having their moments, but failing to convert their chances.

It was more of the same in the second half and those missed opportunities would come back to bite the Lilywhites as Draper headed in Andrei Coubis' long throw in the 81st minute.

The Imps are now unbeaten in their last four league games, while Preston's nightmare start to the season continued with three points from the first 21 available.

Paul Heckingbottom's side started on the front foot, putting in a flurry of crosses into the Lincoln box.

However, it was the visitors who delivered the most meaningful cross in the early stages when Reeco Hackett hung one up for Rob Street whose header deflected behind.

The hosts almost had the lead inadvertently following Andrija Vukcevic's cross, which was heading into the top corner but for an acrobatic save from George Wickens.

One then fell for Johnny Kenny inside the area, but he blazed over. Stanley Mills later tried his luck and saw his effort well saved by Wickens.

Kenny had another opportunity when he came sliding in to meet Alfie Devine's cross from close range and was a whisker away, but was just unable to get there.

Preston were getting closer and their most likely route appeared to be from crosses as Liam Gibbs whipped one in that was just centimetres too high for Callum Lang, before the former then dragged a shot just wide.

The second half continued in the same vein as the home side continued to bombard Lincoln's box with crosses. Lang met one at the far post that came off Wickens' foot and behind, before Kenny tried his luck and tested Wickens again.

The Imps were limited to playing on the break, but still had their chances. Conor McGrandles had a shot saved by Daniel Iversen, and shortly after the Scot clipped one in that was a fraction too high for Ben House at the far post.

House then found himself in a bit of space inside the box and his ball across cannoned on to the body of Harry Clarke, but appeals for a penalty were waved away.

Preston kept pushing as Jordan Storey had one cleared off the line by Dom Jeffries.

But they would be left to rue their missed opportunities late on. Coubis' long throw into the box was met by Draper, whose found the net with the deftest of touches with his head.

The hosts probed late on and continued to put balls into the box, which Lincoln defended resolutely to hold on to three crucial points.

"We're really frustrated. While we're not in front, they're going to have their counter-attacks, opportunities and set plays and 90 per cent of the time we dealt with it, but ultimately it was their biggest weapon.

"While we're not getting in front, they're going to have their opportunities - counter-attacks and set plays.

"There's no lack of effort there. We had opportunities, but we didn't force the big moments to go our way. But that's something we have to put that right, the only way to stop that noise at the end of games is to win games.

"They defended their box really well and they were the ones who forced a scrappy goal in at the other end.

"I can't be critical of the effort of the players, but we are missing that - what Lincoln did today - being the ones that force the ball in. The margins are so fine."

"Our supporters want full throttle football and that's what we're trying to give them. We take lots of learning from the top teams and try and replicate our version of it.

"We've built this success over the last few years on the real ugly side of football, and we're very proud of how we play.

"We've recruited, nurtured and developed a set of players that have got incredible character like I've never seen before in my time in the game. We pride ourselves on those horrible, ugly things.

"If you saw our training ground, it's very competitive and we have a lot of 0-0 draws in training because the lads defend the cage so well, so we pride ourselves on that.

"All the other stuff will come over time and we will be threatening at this level. There were glimpses of that today and Freddie gets the goal he deserves."

articles.title: Blackburn Rovers 3-1 Millwall: Oladapo Afolayan scores twice in victory
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Blackburn Rovers and Millwall at Ewood Park on Saturday; Oladapo Afolayan scores twice as Tony Mowbray's side return to winning ways.
articles.body:
The game hadn't kicked off before the first 'Venky's out' chants could be heard but Afolayan, who turned 29 on Friday, gave the home fans something to cheer with a deft improvised flick to open the scoring in the 41st minute.

Although Lydon Dykes' penalty levelled matters six minutes after the restart, Afolayan's thumping strike around the hour mark restored the lead.

Rovers managed the closing stages well and substitute Andri Gudjohnsen made the game safe in stoppage time with a breakaway goal to end a four-game winless run.

Millwall suffered their third league defeat in four, but will rue the header Dykes planted wide midway through the half.

The Lions made the more assured start but their only chance of note came in the 11th minute when Balazs Toth saved Camiel Neghli's low volley.

Todd Cantwell's snapshot forced Max Crocombe into a smart save but he could do nothing as Rovers went ahead.

Sam Morsy was given too much space just inside the area and though his shot lacked direction, Afolayan's ingenious flick steered the ball into the Millwall net from close range for his first league goal for the club.

The hosts made a disastrous start to the half when substitute Gady Beyuku's first contribution was to bring down Tairyk Arconte in the area after the attacker had stolen in behind on the left.

Dykes took responsibility from the spot and made no mistake, slamming his third of the season down the middle.

But Rovers responded in the 58th minute through Afolayan, who was given time and space to race forward from the centre circle, evading one challenge before rifling a left-foot shot into the bottom corner from 18 yards.

Arconte had the ball in the net after a long throw but the referee saw a foul in the melee.

Millwall continued to threaten and spurned two chances, both created by their full-backs.

First, Zak Sturge's low cross found Arconte, who could only divert wide on the stretch, before Mark Sykes sent in a superb right-wing cross that Dykes headed wide from close range.

Arconte threatened again in the 73rd minute when he turned Tom Atcheson inside out and raced into the area but Hayden Carter crucially deflected his effort over.

Tony Mowbray's side repelled the threats and struck the last blow in a counter started and finished by Gudjohnsen, who shielded the ball and released Jayden Fevrier who squared for the Icelandic striker to slot his third of the season into the bottom corner.

"I remember Afolayan playing for Bolton and he was really direct, positive and aggressive. He's a really bright and intelligent kid who loves football.

"He has an opinion on everything. Overly intelligent sometimes because overly intelligent people have an opinion on everything don't they? You might not always agree with them but that's what Dapo is and I like him because of that.

"When I say to him 'you're not working hard enough, when you lose it you've got to react', he has an answer and knows what I'm talking about. So I feel as though I can connect with him to make him the best version of himself because he understands.

"I like Dapo and that position (on the left), something we were potentially looking at, I'm more than happy with Dapo. He has got aspects he needs to learn and work on but he's a very intelligent kid and there's scope to get better out of him."

"The fourth official told me it (disallowed goal) was for Cooper holding which is incredible really because both of them are standing waiting for the ball to come in.

"Naturally you don't stand with your arms behind your side. I thought it was really soft.

"I thought it was for something in the box beyond the flick so for it to be for Coops holding which is what he said. But you know what it's like. Moments decide matches and I thought today summed that up.

"I didn't think there was a dominant team in the game. I didn't think we were great, I didn't think they were great, I just thought they were more clinical in moments than what we were during the match and sometimes at this level, that's the difference.

"Over the last 19-20 months since I've been here, we've been brilliant in both boxes. Unfortunately today, we weren't."

articles.title: Watford 1-2 Stoke City: Jack McGlynn and Eric Bocat score in Potters win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Watford and Stoke City at Vicarage Road on Saturday; Jack McGlynn and Eric Bocat score as Mark Robins' resurgent Potters claim victory.
articles.body:
A 1-1 draw at Cardiff in midweek had ended a sequence of nine consecutive defeats away from Staffordshire, and the Potters were good value for their first win in 11 road trips - and their third success in four Championship games.

McGlynn opened the scoring for Stoke on half-time with Eric Bocat doubling the lead 13 minutes into the second half. Amin Nabizada's reply came too late for the Hornets.

Fortified by 10 summer signings, including United States international McGlynn from Houston Dynamo and £10million former Manchester United academy midfielder Ethan Galbraith from Swansea, Stoke were superior until they survived a late scare.

In the opening eight minutes alone Bocat, in plentiful space, sliced wastefully wide from 10 yards out and the French defender's cross was headed down, but over the top, by Lamine Cisse.

Then Galbraith tested home keeper Federico Ravaglia, the Italian making a sharp low save, as Watford struggled to break the Potters' press.

It took the Hornets 35 minutes to register a goal attempt of any description, Othmane Maamma firing a speculative volley way off target to end Stoke's monopoly of 10 shots without reply.

The home side went close when Ukraine international Maksym Talovierov's last-ditch challenge thwarted Mamadou Doumbia, diverting his fierce effort over the top.

But Watford, already depleted by a glut of injuries, were further disrupted by full-back Jordan Zemura's withdrawal before half-time and they could not make it through to the interval unscathed.

Lamine Cisse had already had a goal discounted for offside before McGlynn struck in the last seconds of added time, firing high and handsome beyond Ravaglia from the edge of the box to give the visitors a deserved lead.

Livewire McGlynn, signed on deadline day for a reported £4 million, kept Watford's hard-pressed defence under pressure with his set-piece delivery and his double act with Galbraith was outstanding.

Stoke continued to call the tune after the break, Cisse rattling the underside of the bar before Northern Ireland midfielder Justin Devenny shovelled a glorious chance wide from Ben Johnson's low centre.

But they were on course for the points when Bocat broke through the inside left channel and fired low across Ravaglia into the far corner to double the Potters' lead 12 minutes into the second period.

Watford lacked energy, cohesion and, crucially, options to change the course of the game from the bench, where head coach Alessio Dionisi named two goalkeepers, two right-backs, two centre-forwards and no midfielders among his eight substitutes.

Former West Ham striker Michail Antonio, who signed a one-year deal on Friday, was among Dionisi's replacements but his last appearance in English football was back in December 2024 and he was effectively included as window dressing.

Substitute Nabizada's brilliant, curling 25-yard effort, his third goal of the season, reduced the deficit on the stroke of 90 minutes, and Stoke then had to live on their nerves for six minutes of stoppage time before ending their 251-day wait for an away win.

"My players are tired - it's normal when you play every three days for 10 matches, and we are a good team when we have them all (available), but I know our situation.

"If we stick together and we believe in the future, I'm sure the future will be better.

"Amin has scored three goals and I'm very happy for him, but we need other players to help because it is impossible for him to arrive at 10 goals (for the season) - I hope he does, but it will be difficult. The players need to reassert themselves."

"It's been a long time coming. It was a really good performance, but no-one gets carried away. We have to grab hold of it and make sure we are getting better all the time.

"It's all about players and their quality. Our players showed they have quality. They have to carry out a game plan and be brave. They were all of those things. They made it work. It's a testament to them.

"Jack's a really good lad - very humble and really excited to be in England and playing in the Championship, but he's under no illusions that we want to do better and better.

"We had a long, long time last season with a lot of players out and we couldn't find a way of picking up points to keep our season alive.

"We wanted to change that. The owner has been fantastic and backed us incredibly well again. Now we have a decent balance and the makings of a really enjoyable team to watch.

"This team has been put together only very recently, so they deserve a lot of credit for taking information on very quickly - and this isn't the finished product. We've picked up 10 points from 12 after a poor start and it's a really good step forward and a really good spot to be in."

articles.title: Swansea City 3-1 Burnley: Struggling Clarets beaten again
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Swansea City and Burnley at the Swansea.com Stadium on Saturday; Adam Idah, Moussa Yeo and Zan Vipotnik steer Swans to victory over the struggling Clarets.
articles.body:
The victory took Vitor Matos' side level on points with West Ham at the top of the table and erased the memory of the 3-1 midweek mauling at Southampton. For Burnley, it was a fourth defeat in seven league games and they are still awaiting their first win.

Both goals they conceded in the first half were avoidable and had their shooting been more precise they could have been at least on level terms.

Hayen was able to include former Leicester and England striker Jamie Vardy in his matchday squad for the first time following the 39-year-old's transfer from Serie A side Cremonese.

He finally made his debut as a 64th-minute substitute and had the ball in the Swansea net nine minutes later only to have the goal ruled out for offside.

Burnley started well enough and the first chance of the game fell to striker Zeki Amdouni in the eighth minute.

Having held off Stephen Welsh in the race for a ball into the Swansea box he then shot into the side-netting from a good angle.

The home side opened the scoring in the 14th minute when Adam Idah grabbed his third goal of the season. Chasing a long ball through the centre he first held off Igor Julio and then ran on to challenge Burnley goalkeeper Max Weiss just outside his box.

Weiss waited too long, lost the ball when challenged by Idah and then had to watch the striker calmly stroke the ball into an empty net.

Worse followed in the 33rd minute after Burnley had had a significant period of pressure.

But when their third corner in a row was cleared, Ugo Raghouber gave the ball away and Elijah Just picked it up in the centre circle before sending Moussa Yeo on a solo run at goal from halfway.

He got to the edge of the area before putting the ball into the bottom-left corner to notch his first goal in a Swansea shirt.

Despite going two goals down, Burnley created a number of chances and Aaron Ramsey forced Lawrence Vigouroux into a brilliant one-handed save as he tipped his rasping shot onto the crossbar.

The visitors finally scored in the 58th minute when Largie Ramazani beat the offside trap and fired past Vigouroux with a low shot into the left corner. That gave the Clarets renewed hope of getting something out of the game, but Swansea added a third goal five minutes later.

Marco Stamenic threaded the ball through for Ronald to chase and after outpacing Lucas Pires he pulled the ball across the box to give Zan Vipotnik the easiest of tap ins.

Burnley had the ball in the Swansea net once again in the 87th minute from an inswinging corner but referee James Bell spotted interference on Vigouroux and ruled it out.

"It was a good game for us and it was quite complete in different phases. We had really good moments when we had the ball, important moments that gave us the initiative and control in the right positions.

"That allowed us to push Burnley back and deep.

"Nothing has changed for us. The most important thing is that we keep focusing on the process, on what we can improve, when we need to improve and then on the games.

"Then the results will speak for themselves. We need to keep improving our game and individually."

"It's a must-win game for us against Derby. There are no excuses, but there are clear reasons for our current situation.

"We're missing a lot of players and several new signings do not yet have the match fitness we need.

"I mentioned a few weeks ago that we had to survive until the international break, where we can finally work properly on the training pitch.

"But surviving means taking points and winning games, which we haven't managed to do enough. That makes this a difficult period, but Saturday is a must-win.

"Despite the results, we are growing as a team. What we desperately need is one victory to reward the performance and rebuild confidence.

"One win will change a lot for us - everyone is craving that feeling again. You can hold me accountable for not winning games, but there are also realistic factors such as injuries, lack of fitness and integrating new signings late.

"I'll keep working exactly as I always do. I treat every game as if it were my last, because that keeps you sharp and injects energy into the squad and tomorrow I will put that energy back into the group."

articles.title: Middlesbrough 4-3 Norwich City: Ashley Phillips scores late Boro winner in thriller
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Middlesbrough and Norwich City at the Riverside Stadium on Saturday; Ashley Phillips seals late victory for Boro in a seven-goal thriller.
articles.body:
The Canaries, looking for a third win on the bounce, made the perfect start with just 50 seconds on the clock when striker Mohamed Toure hammered in, but within six more minutes Boro had gone ahead.

Sebastian Berhalter, signed from Vancouver Whitecaps this summer, powered in his first Middlesbrough goal to level things.

Exciting winger Amario Cozier-Duberry, making his first league start since arriving on loan from Brighton, then got the Riverside crowd bouncing with a tidy finish a few minutes later.

And Norwich fell further behind when Berhalter added his second in the 36th sixth minute to put Kim Hellberg's side in the driving seat.

Norwich fought back when Jovon Makama's predatory finish 20 minutes from time was followed by an equaliser from fellow substitute Jacob Wright five minutes later.

However, defender Phillips - with his first league career goal after arriving from Tottenham - popped up in the area with the killer blow to secure a third straight home win for Middlesbrough.

Norwich got things rolling early on after Andre Brooks brilliantly kept the ball in play. Alfie Jones was outmuscled by Toure before he fired powerfully in off the far post.

Less than three minutes later Berhalter levelled. The American hammered a finish in off the underside of the crossbar after a horrible turn from Ruairi McConville allowed Tommy Conway and Will Lankshear to create the opening.

Middlesbrough claimed the lead less than three minutes later in style.

A precise cross-field ball from Berhalter was chested down exquisitely by Conway. He ran at his marker before squaring to Cozier-Duberry, who curled a low finish inside Vladan Kovacevic's bottom right corner.

There were chances at both ends after that but Middlesbrough, after goalkeeper Radek Vitek had made a fine one-handed stop to deny Brooks, extended their advantage before the break.

It was Berhalter again who was in the right place to turn Callum Brittain's scuffed shot beyond a wrong-footed Kovacevic.

After the restart chances were more limited until Norwich introduced their substitutes.

Wright and Makama combined for the latter to beat Vitek and pull a goal back in the 70th minute, and they had the hope they needed.

Soon after Wright had levelled himself. He was left in acres of space to find Anthony Musaba. After the winger's shot was saved, Wright was in place to turn the loose ball high into the net.

However, Middlesbrough were not finished either. Phillips completed the scoring in the dying seconds, capitalising on Lankshear's pass across the area to secure a dramatic three points.

"If you look at the game as a neutral, it was a fantastic game. This was two teams that does everything they can to win the game.

"In that way it was a fantastic game, there was a lot of quality, the best version of football that I like - two teams going at each other is brilliant.

"We were the better team over 90 minutes, even though we played a very strong team. I am happy with that and it was down to the character of the boys and getting the win when things weren't going our way second half.

"The strong thing for this group is how they support each other. I see so many who were outside the squad who today celebrated like it was important for them; that is not always how it is but this group is fantastic like that.

"I need to help the players know what we should do better to win the games. Game management is a massive thing. The character of the players won us the game."

" It was a frantic game, with two teams really going to win.

"The biggest disappointment was not the first goal against but the 30 minutes after. I saw two/three players starting to doubt, they were not brave enough on the ball. We didn't show the football we can play.

"I wanted to see another phase of the team (after half-time) and we then showed our qualities - the team did brilliantly. The biggest memory of this game was how good we can be if everyone goes full.

"It felt like a boxing fight. I felt Middlesbrough were on the ropes in the last 10 minutes, but in the dying seconds we got the punch where we go down and we lose.

"But I'm proud of what my team showed in the second half. We will have a good season if we do that in the next days and months.

"Everyone who watched the game will have enjoyed the game - seven goals. But I'm gutted now that we don't get points from this game because we deserved this."
