articles.title: Charlton Athletic 0-0 Portsmouth: Goalless at The Valley
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Charlton Athletic and Portsmouth at The Valley on Saturday; Nathan Jones' Addicks and John Mousinho's Pompey play out a goalless draw.
articles.body:
The Championship encounter may have lacked goals, but it was not devoid of entertainment, particularly in an open second half.

The hosts were the better side in the opening 45 minutes and had the big chances to break the deadlock.

Millenic Alli, who spent the second half of last season on loan with the visitors, volleyed over from close range from a perfect left-wing cross by Tyreece Campbell in the 32nd minute.

That came soon after Portsmouth goalkeeper Daniel Bielica used his legs to repel a fierce strike from Karlan Grant at his near post.

Portsmouth captain Marlon Pack needed to make a crucial header out for a corner from an early Campbell cross.

The visitors, who came into the contest having scored in their last 11 away league matches, did not have a shot on target before the interval.

Charlton keeper Arthur Okonkwo needed to be alert in the 15th minute, sticking out a leg to cut out Terry Devlin's low cutback after slick approach play.

Conor Shaughnessy came to the away team's rescue when he hooked the ball away from his own goal-line after Addicks loanee Tyler Bindon had nodded a deep cross back into a dangerous area.

Alli, booed by the travelling support every time he got on the ball, had the last chance of the half but hit a 20-yard effort straight at Bielica.

Okonkwo needed all of his long frame to dive low to his left and get a hand to Abu Kamara's shot just 20 seconds into the second period.

Portsmouth had a full week to prepare for the match and they looked fresher and stronger as Charlton, who drew 0-0 with QPR on Wednesday night, began to show signs of fatigue.

Referee Andrew Kitchen was unimpressed by Jayden Meghoma's penalty claims, the left-back appealing for a pull on the arm by Alli.

Oliver Skipp produced a fine recovery tackle to slide in and dispossess Adrian Segecic on the edge of the area after Bindon had turned over possession.

Adrian Segecic wastefully shot tamely at Okonkwo from inside the area before Colby Bishop failed to apply a sliding close-range finish to Ryan Kavuma-McQueen's inviting cross in the 81st minute.

Charlton dug deep into their reserves as time ticked down.

Conor Coventry curled over from a Charlton corner that was played short and worked across the edge of the area.

Shaughnessy produced a crucial defensive block from a shot by Grant and there were big appeals from the home support for a penalty when Miles Leaburn went down after a coming together with Benjamin Arthur.

"The performance was really good, especially in the first half. We created some excellent chances, looked a threat and controlled the game.

"When you look at the game we had against them here last season, it was the polar opposite. Our midfield two were excellent and our wide ones carried a threat.

"We had the absolute clear-cut chance of the game. If we had scored the first goal, especially in the first half, then we are very difficult to beat here.

"There probably won't be an easier chance in the Football League today than Mille Alli's chance. He is three yards out. He just needs to guide it on target and he scores. He managed to put it over.

"Karlan Grant has had a great chance. It was a really good game, end to end and two really committed sides. Portsmouth beat us twice last season, so it is a better result than we had last year.

"Overall the performance level was there and it's a clean sheet. You can see some partnerships building.

"We want to get all our injured players back. We had Charlie Kelman back today and hopefully we get Josh Edwards back next week, so that is another one.

"We will be in a stronger position after the international break. The five defenders have had to go from the Tottenham game until now, really putting in proper shifts. To keep three clean sheets shows that."

"You come away from home and draw 0-0, then a clean sheet is the really positive aspect of the game.

"We created some really good chances in the second half but just didn't put the ball in the net. Mixed emotions, because we could have won it.

"We got into some good spots but didn't really test the goalkeeper in the first half. With Charlton playing Wednesday night we thought we'd have more joy as the game opened up, which we did.

"There are some really good signs, but we need to keep improving.

"We put the chances in the back of the net last week. We didn't do it this week. The top end of the pitch, we have got quality and goals there, which I think will come."

articles.standfirst: El conjunto rojillo cayó prácticamente sin oposición ante el Espanyol en El Sadar
articles.summary: El conjunto rojillo cayó prácticamente sin oposición ante el Espanyol en El Sadar
articles.body: Hay días en los que, cuando todo puede salir mal, sale mal. Así se podría resumir la primera parte de Osasuna frente al Espanyol. El cuadro navarro se puso por detrás en el marcador en apenas tres minutos, reclamó un posible penalti sobre Raúl García de Haro que no se señaló, Catena volvió a cometer por segunda jornada consecutiva un error de bulto que supuso el 0-2 y, por si fuera poco, Rubén García recortó distancias y el gol fue anulado posteriormente cuando se revisó que el balón había salido anteriormente por escasos centímetros del campo. Todo ello, al margen de los errores, tiene su parte de salir constantemente la cruz de la moneda. Sin embargo, la segunda parte no tiene excusa alguna. Un Osasuna plano, sin ofrecimientos, inoperante, inofensivo y lento fue víctima de un Espanyol férreo, bien colocado, atento y con la motivación de preservar una ventaja de dos a modo de tesoro. Algo inadmisible para el equipo navarro, más aún delante de su gente. En definitiva, un segundo tiempo donde el marcador obliga a quemar las naves derivó en un ejercicio de impotencia inexplicable. Con esta derrota, el conjunto rojillo suma otra decepción a la “manita” encajada ante el Alavés y acerca fantasmas del pasado a causa del juego y no tanto de los términos clasificatorios, marcados por un excelente arranque de campaña.

articles.title: After fumble-return TD was negated because Virginia Tech defender dropped ball before goal line, Hokies return another fumble for TD on next play
articles.summary: Ball don't lie?
articles.body:
It's only Week 2, but Virginia Tech produced one of the wildest defensive sequences you'll see over the entirety of the 2026 college football season on Saturday.

Late in the first half — with the Hokies already up 10-0 — Aycen Stevens sacked Old Dominion quarterback Quinn Henicle and forced a fumble. Keon Wylie picked up the ball and returned it 55 yards for a touchdown … but dropped the ball before he crossed the goal line.

It didn't even look like Wylie was celebrating too early, either. He simply just had the ball fall out of his hands as he shifted the ball from his left to his right.

The touchback gave Old Dominion the ball at its own 20-yard line and, well, Henicle was sacked again. And he fumbled again. This time, Mylachi Williams forced the fumble, and Tyson Flowers picked it up. And Flowers held onto the ball as he crossed the goal line for a 17-0 Virginia Tech lead.

If you believe the ball doesn't lie, then the second touchdown might have been a ball-don't-lie moment for you. And it was a clear sign that Old Dominion probably wasn't going to beat the Hokies for a second straight season. ODU took down Virginia Tech 45-26 a season ago, as the Hokies struggled through a disappointing season that ultimately led to the hire of former Penn State coach James Franklin.

articles.title: Vitor Matos: Swansea City have shown they can beat any Championship opponent
articles.summary: Vitor Matos believes Swansea City's bright start to the new season proves they are capable of competing with any team in the Championship.
articles.body:
Vitor Matos believes Swansea City's bright start to the new season proves they are capable of competing with any team in the Championship.

Swansea climbed back to second in the table – behind leaders West Ham on goal difference – thanks to Saturday's 3-1 victory over struggling Burnley.

Adam Idah, Moussa Yeo and Zan Vipotnik all found the target as the Swans produced the ideal response following their first league defeat at Southampton in midweek.

After beating Burnley, Matos claimed that he did not know where Swansea are in the league table – but reckons his new-look squad have shown they can cut it in the second tier.

"I think we have a team who can compete against every team in the league," the Swansea head coach said.

"That's what we want. When we can compete against everyone, we know that on that day, at that particular time, we can have a proper performance and beat any opponent.

"If that happens all the time, we don't know, but we will work our socks off for that."

Latest Swansea City news, analysis and fan views

Listen to the latest Swansea City interviews, news and discussion on BBC Sounds

Swansea finished 11th in the Championship last season, with Matos inspiring an upturn in fortunes after a slump in form had prompted relegation concerns before he took charge in November 2025.

A promising start to the new campaign – on the back of a busy summer transfer window – means there is a growing optimism that Swansea could have a say in the promotion race.

West Ham have been showered with praise in the wake of their emphatic win over Wrexham on Friday, yet the Swans are keeping pace with the Hammers after seven league games.

When asked about being level with Nuno Espirito Santo's promotion favourites, Matos said: "Nothing has changed for us.

"I think the most important thing is that we keep focus on the process, on what we can improve when we need to improve.

"Then the results will speak for themselves, like last season."

articles.title: El Milan iguala un 2-0 ante la Lazio después de cambiar a Modric al descanso
articles.standfirst: La entrada en el descanso de Diego Moreira, autor de un doblete, cambió el partido
articles.summary: La entrada en el descanso de Diego Moreira, autor de un doblete, cambió el partido
articles.body: Partido raro en el Olímpico, con una parte para cada equipo. El Milan consiguió rescatar un punto ante la Lazio (2-2) después de que Rúben Amorim sorprendiera retirando a Luka Modric al descanso, con 2-0 en contra. El Milan se diluyó nada más empezar, justo después de que Mandas desviara un cabezazo de Chukwueze en el 3', tras un buen centro de Modric desde la izquierda. Un paradón de Maignan en el 5' a disparo de Zaccagni y otra intervención del meta galo a remate de Noslin en el 7' avisaron de lo que estaba por venir. Abrió a banda Nuno Tavares para Mattia Zaccagni. El centro de éste al segundo palo lo marcó Matteo Cancellieri, anticipando a Estupiñan, para marcar el 1-0 en el 10'. Maignan negó el 2-0 a Zaccagni en el 21', pero nada pudo hacer para evitar el gol de Tijjani Noslin en el 39'. Taylor centró desde la izquierda y el neerlandés se jugó la cabeza para marcar sobre la línea después de que su primer intento se estrellara en el larguero. Entraron Pulisic, Musah y Diego Moreira al descanso por Loftus-Cheek, Modric y Estupiñan y lo cierto es que el Milan mejoró. Mandas se tuvo que emplear a fondo para detener un cabezazo de Pavlovic en el 57' y un tiro abajo de Pulisic en el 60'. El que realmente cambió el partido fue Diego Moreira, que se llevó el 'MVP'. El ex del Estrasburgo, fichado a cambio de 50 millones de euros, recortó distancias en el 65' al reventar con la zurda un centro pasado de Pulisic desde la derecha. Dos minutos después, en el 67', anotó el 2-2. Robó Musah, centró y Rabiot cedió atrás para que Diego Moreira, otra vez, batiera a Mandas con un disparo raso cruzado. El punto era justo, pero el Milan rozó el triunfo con un disparo de Cisse que salió rozando el palo largo en el 77' y un disparo de Diego Moreira al lateral de la red en el 80'. El 'hat-trick' hubiera sido la guinda a su descomunal partido.

articles.body:
Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner, speaking to BBC Match of the Day: "I'm really proud of the team's performance and the spirit they showed. We did better after 10 or 15 minutes but we were a little bit impatient in the final third.

"We were too impatient and eager. It was a little bit up and down. In the second half we moved the ball quicker and switched from left to right and we saw the confidence grow.

" Liam Delap 's hit didn't surprise me because I see it in training. That's what a striker should do. I feel this goal gave him a lot of confidence because he was a lot more present. It was a top team performance."

Nottingham Forest striker Igor Jesus, who scored the 88th-minute winner: "It's our first win in the Premier League this season and we know how important it is for us. It's very important for us and we need to keep it going. I just want to say thank you to everyone who came to support us today."

Four of Liam Delap's 14 Premier League goals have come against Aston Villa , his most against a single opponent in the competition.

Morgan Gibbs-White has either scored or assisted in each of his last eight Premier League away appearances (six goals, four assists).

articles.title: Aston Villa: Unai Emery searching for answers after defeat by Nottingham Forest.
articles.summary: Aston Villa have lost three of their opening four Premier League games to leave boss Unai Emery struggling for answers.
articles.body:
Defender Tyrone Mings summed up the Aston Villa mood as he slumped to the floor at full-time following a 2-1 defeat at home to Nottingham Forest .

Three defeats in their opening four games only leaves further questions for manager Unai Emery to answer following a summer rebuild.

Villa may have ended a run of 372 Premier League minutes without a Premier League goal but their problems remain.

If Coventry beat Brighton on Sunday, Emery's side will sit bottom of the table.

It is the fourth time they have started a top-flight season without winning any of their opening four games, having done so in 1992-93, 1997-98 and 2025-26.

It mirrors last season - which ended with a fourth-placed Premier League finish and historic Europe League triumph - but those celebrations from May already feel like a lifetime ago.

Jesus hands Forest first win at Villa in 32 years

Emery questions why McAtee was not sent off

A late Igor Jesus winner meant Oliver Glasner is now unbeaten in his eight games against Emery and, after a first win as Forest boss, he will view this as one of the sweetest.

Liam Delap scored just 45 seconds after the restart and, while Alysson levelled for Villa with his first goal in English football, the visitors were deserved winners.

Jesus pounced ahead of Aaron Wan-Bissaka with two minutes left to earn a first win at Villa Park since 1994 as Forest took advantage of Villa's misfortune.

By then they were down to 10 men after full-back Ian Maatsen was forced off injured, with Emery using all his substitutes to add to their defensive problems.

There is a fear the left-back's ankle injury could keep him out for a considerable time, meaning new signing Matteo Ruggeri will be called on, perhaps earlier than Emery would want.

The Villa boss complained Forest attacker James McAtee should have been sent off for the challenge which injured Maatsen, but refused to blame it for the outcome of the match.

"When we equalised the match could change but we finished with Ian Maatsen injured and with 10 players, we conceded so many chances in the last minutes and they scored the second goal and deserved it," he said.

"But after watching it on TV, I think the VAR should call the referee because it's a clear tackle behind the player and, for me, it should be a red card.

"Of course, they deserved it (the win), but the decision of the referee should be different. We finished the match in Brighton , two yellow cards for Joao Gomes, and we accepted it. But today, after the injury of Maatsen, and we're finishing with 10.

"He didn't want to injure our player but if we can watch it through the TV, it's a VAR action, and to call the referee and should be a red card, and maybe finishing with 10 v 10 was maybe different in the match.

"But it's not an excuse how we play the second half. We played so so poor, and this is our work and our responsibility or my responsibility."

Centre-back Pau Torres was also replaced in the first half to leave Villa's backline increasingly thin, with summer signing Taylor Harwood-Bellis omitted from the squad again.

Villa visit Coventry in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday before a trip to Tottenham and the £30m centre-back will be expecting a chance at the CBS Arena.

They were unable to cope with a rejuvenated Delap - who also had a goal disallowed - and the visitors had 22 shots.

Glasner's men also had 32 touches in Villa's box as an ineffective home attack struggled again.

Bar a comical scramble, where Victor Lindelof failed to net after a combination of Matz Sels, Murillo and the post denied him, they created little.

Nicolas Jackson was replaced at half-time with his replacement Tammy Abraham - a player Emery wanted to sell this summer - because Emery feared the Senegal striker would get sent off after an early yellow card.

Brazilian Alysson was also introduced and glanced in John McGinn's cross against the run of play, before Johan Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye - the pair costing a combined £98m - made their debuts as second-half substitutes, but were unable to make a difference.

Alejandro Garnacho was again an unused substitute, with the Chelsea loanee so far failing to impress Emery to get game time.

A first win at Villa Park since 1994 was deserved for Forest as the hosts' home record continued to crumble.

They had not lost at home in the league for 12 months before Glasner's former club Crystal Palace won 3-0 last August.

Since then - with Glasner also winning 2-1 with the Eagles in the Carabao Cup - Villa Park has become less of a fortress.

They lost four of their final 15 home league games last season, while also relying on late goals to rescue a point against Leeds and beat Brighton and Sunderland .

A 3-1 FA Cup exit to Newcastle also exposed the frailties at Villa Park, which have continued this season with an opening 1-0 defeat at home to champions Arsenal followed by the loss to Forest.

Along with a new squad after several key departures, the North Stand redevelopment has meant the capacity has been reduced and there are no fans at one end.

But the drop off at home should now be alarming.

Villa won at home when it mattered most at the end of last season - routing Forest in the Europa League semi-final en route to winning the competition and putting four past Liverpool to book a Champions League spot - but they need to rediscover the feeling which made them near-invincible in front of their own followers.

So often over the past few seasons, after a Villa equaliser, they have they gone on to win, but there was no grandstand finish this time, leaving Emery perplexed about why his side could not control the game.

"I don't know why," he said. "I want to see the match again and to understand why we lost our shape."

Jesus instead had the final say to leave the Spaniard, who has provided solutions at Villa for so long during his tenure, searching for answers to revive his side's fortunes.

articles.title: Liverpool star told exactly when a decision will be made on his future
articles.summary: Liverpool still have a fair few things to sort out this season. The Anfield outfit are still nowhere near ready to start challenging for the Premier League t...
articles.body:
Liverpool still have a fair few things to sort out this season.

The Anfield outfit are still nowhere near ready to start challenging for the Premier League title despite their almost £200 million spend in the summer.

Many players have their futures hanging in the balance with some even already looking for potential ways to exit L4 in January.

However, it's not only the potential exit of players that Liverpool need to worry about.

Liverpool won't make a decision on Virgil van Dijk 's future until April 2027

Virgil van Dijk is still one of Liverpool's most important players .

The Dutchman has been the Reds' leader for as long as anyone can remember with the club likely to be much worse off if he wasn't among their ranks.

For years now, he's been the rock of the Anfield outfit's defence with fans hardly able to even vision a Liverpool team without him in it.

However, since his contract is set to expire in June 2027, Liverpool don't really have that long left to figure things out, or, that's what fans believe, anyway.

But, a fresh report from Football Insider has contradicted those thoughts with journalist Pete O'Rourke sharing that Liverpool don't really want to make a final decision on Van Dijk 's future until April 2027.

"The 35-year-old will see his current contract expire in 2027 as things stand, and could be allowed to leave Anfield on a free transfer come the end of the season," they wrote .

"He remains a crucial part of Andoni Iraola 's starting XI for now, but concerns about his age and the club's long-term plans mean no decision has been made yet.

"As I revealed on the latest edition of Football Insider's Transfer Insider podcast, Liverpool will follow a similar path to the last time Van Dijk signed a contract extension.

"In 2025, both Van Dijk and Mohamed Salah put pen to paper on extensions shortly before the end of the season after months of speculation about potential moves away.

"Two years on, Liverpool are once again preparing to hold talks later in the season, with a decision over the captain's future not expected to be made until April at the earliest."

Liverpool must figure out if they want to keep hold of Virgil van Dijk by January

The Anfield outfit may want as much time as possible to judge whether they believe he's worth another two-year extension but, with the form he's been in so far, it's clear that his levels haven't dropped.

Even though he's 35 years old, he is very clearly still the Reds' best centre-back and without him, it's unclear whether Liverpool would even be unbeaten at the moment.

Iraola clearly sees him as a major part of his plans this season so, you'd think that if the Spaniard is sticking around for a while that he'd want his favoured players to stay put.

Obviously, we're only a few games into the 2026-27 campaign so things could change but, Liverpool without Van Dijk is a very scary thought at the moment.

Especially since they already need to upgrade many other areas of their squad.

articles.title: Chelsea’s ‘soft’ problem is becoming impossible for Xabi Alonso’s luxury attack to solve
articles.summary: Chelsea 2-2 Hull City: Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro scored for the hosts either side of a first-half brace by Algeria’s Mohamed Belloumi
articles.body:
In the end, Chelsea clung on for a brave point. Emiliano Martinez made an important late save. They survived a barrage of set-pieces. And when Cole Palmer stood over a free-kick 30 yards from goal, with the last kick of the game, he pumped it into the stands just to be safe. A draw against a team who were, for much of the afternoon, top of the league? You have to take it.

Of course that wasn't quite the mood at Stamford Bridge when the final whistle blew on this 2-2 draw. A volley of boos rang out and it was hard to know exactly who they were for. The players, perhaps, who were collectively disconnected and at times individually calamitous. The referee, Farai Hallam, who at one point intercepted a Chelsea counterattack with his feet and picked up the ball with his hands, like a schoolteacher at the end of break time. Chelsea were exasperated when he waved away several handball shouts.

But really it was an outpouring of frustration, that as talented a front three as Chelsea possess, they cannot possibly outscore a defence as chaotic and porous as this one. Chelsea have conceded at least two goals in all four Premier League games this season, 13 goals in six games in all competitions, and that is too much for Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers to overcome every weekend. Arsenal , by comparison, have conceded only once .

Chelsea went from 1-0 up to 2-1 down in six minutes, and Xabi Alonso accused his players of "soft" defending. "We are attacking better than defending," he understated. "It's just four games, but the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don't like it, and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls – this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better."

Perhaps there was also some confusion mixed into the fans' outpouring, after a game when Alonso's team didn't always make sense. Why was Maxence Lacroix not at the heart of defence from the start? Why doesn't the manager trust Estevao Willian when Chelsea are chasing a game? What exactly is the purpose of Malo Gusto ?

The first Hull goal was particularly troubling from Chelsea's perspective. Wesley Fofana watched a long ball fly over his head, Gusto lost a 50-50 in the corner and Jorrel Hato lost his senses, misjudging the flight of the cross like it was his first time encountering this strange bouncing sphere. Mohamed Belloumi couldn't believe his luck as the ball hopped over Hato, and he took the opportunity beautifully with a low drive under Martinez's body.

Moments before Hull's second, it was quite obvious to everyone in the stadium before the corner was taken that Belloumi was alone in a sunny glade on the edge of the box. He pleaded for a pass which didn't come, and yet still had no Chelsea player near him by the time the ball flew into the middle, bounced off the bar and rolled out to his feet. This time his finish took a couple of fortunate deflections, but you couldn't say Hull deserved any less.

Martinez did not have his finest afternoon. He flapped at the corner which led to Belloumi's second goal, and in the second half fumbled a routine shot which almost presented the ball to Oli McBurnie to tap in what would have most probably been the winner.

Another recruit from Aston Villa with improvements to make is Austin MacPhee, Chelsea's hirsute set-piece coach, who bobbed around the technical area waving his arms and looking generally exasperated with players who apparently weren't following his instructions, as if somehow that wasn't his fault. Some of Chelsea's intricate attacking corners almost worked, when Palmer would ghost to the front post and receive a low pass, but they need to spend time on the defensive side.

These are early days, of course. Alonso is still learning his best combinations. Chelsea will be better when Moises Caicedo returns, when Marco Palestra finally begins his career here. But for all their successful trading, earning a billion pounds in sales since BlueCo took over, there was a sense that some past players were missing. Trevoh Chalobah , for example, was Chelsea's best defender for large parts of last season and would surely have enhanced this ragged display.

The only positive is that their attack continues to fire. Rogers and Pedro produced clinical finishes in each half, and while it wasn't Palmer's best game, he played a major hand in both goals. Palmer has a habit of drifting to the fringes when it becomes congested, partly out of an instinctive feeling of where the space is, where the opponents' soft spots are, and partly out of frustration at a lack of involvement. He loitered on the left and then drove into the box to feed Pedro, who lashed a first-time finish into the roof of the net.

But they could not find another, and if anything it was Hull who looked most likely to score a third. No Premier League team have been involved in as many goals as Chelsea so far this season, but Alonso would much rather they were not the top flight's great entertainers.

"I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we won," he said. "For sure, it's some repeated patterns that we are making. It will take time to fix them. When we get the lead, you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back.

"Especially in the first goal, we can do much better. It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances … It was from a long ball, two bounces. The way it happened, you need to be very, very aware, and very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished."

articles.title: Barcelona teenage prospect makes promising start with youth team after summer move
articles.summary: Having arrived at the club in the summer, Mikael Baza has made an encouraging first impression at Barcelona after getting his first minutes in the club’s you...
articles.body:
Having arrived at the club in the summer, Mikael Baza has made an encouraging first impression at Barcelona after getting his first minutes in the club's youth set-up.

The 16-year-old defender is already showing some of the qualities that convinced Barça to invest in him.

According to SPORT , Baza made his Barcelona debut against Vic a few days ago before featuring again on Friday against the senior side of Atletic Sant Just.

The second match provided a particularly demanding test because many of his opponents were older and physically more developed.

Barcelona lost 2-1, with Atletic Sant Just's greater experience and physical maturity making a difference, but Baza's individual performance was viewed positively.

The left-footed centre-back looked strong when stepping into challenges, quick when covering space behind the defence and comfortable physically despite only recently joining his new team-mates.

Mikael Baza is a developmental bet by Barcelona. (Photo by Christof Koepsel/Getty Images for DFB)

His quality in possession also stood out. Baza showed confidence when bringing the ball out from the back, an especially important trait for a young defender hoping to progress through Barcelona's system.

At more than 1.90 metres tall, Baza combines size with a naturally left-footed profile, something that makes him particularly interesting from a squad-building perspective.

Barcelona's recruitment department has increasingly focused on identifying young players before competition from Europe's biggest clubs becomes impossible to manage.

Baza fits that strategy alongside other recent additions , including Hamza Abdelkarim, Jesse Bisiwu, Josue Caicedo, Patricio Pacifico and Ajay Tavares.

The club are not expecting immediate first-team football, however. Baza has only just begun his first season at youth level and is still adapting to La Masia .

Deco and Joao Amaral have done an excellent job of setting up the scouting network that gives Barça an early advantage.

For a very long time, Barcelona almost exclusively depended on La Masia when it came to youngsters coming into the first team.

Deco and Amaral have signed gems like Hamza Abdelkarim in the recent past. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

However, Deco and Amaral have understood that, in this increasingly inflated market, it is important for them to stay ahead of the curve.

The likes of Hamza and Bisiwu already look like great business, and if Baza can keep up his good start, it will not be long before he joins that list.

It remains to be seen how Baza's development pans out and whether he becomes a player Barcelona can count on in the coming years.

articles.title: How Inter’s Andy Diouf bewitched Zinedine Zidane amidst possible France call-up
articles.summary: Serie A side Inter have seen Andy Diouf emerge as one of their best players so far this season. This has led to him attracting attention from new France boss...
articles.body:
Serie A side Inter have seen Andy Diouf emerge as one of their best players so far this season. This has led to him attracting attention from new France boss Zinedine Zidane, who has included him amongst the pre-called up players for Les Bleus .

La Gazzetta dello Sport note that the versatile wing-back's performance against Real Madrid has played a key role in this.

He was constantly causing problems on his side, taking Marc Cucurella on and even defensive, proved a tough nut to crack for Vinicius Jr.

His desire to be very direct and also create from that side has caught particular attention. Diouf also has two Serie A assists and has pretty much cemented his spot on the right wing-back position.

Initially signed to bolster the midfield, the idea of turning Diouf into a wing-back was burn in pre-season. Cristian Chivu had dabbled with the idea last season but could never quite implement it during the campaign.

His ability to carry the ball is specifically turning into an advantage for that role. That is one reason why he was seen as a good fit and things are clearly working well. It is a role which suits him and even if he may not exactly make a debut for France, it is a sign that things are going in the right direction.
